sections.heading: Access
sections.text: When entering the Glacier boss room, one has a 50 percent chance to see a tunnel blocked by rock on the right hand side. Once the boss is defeated, a cage appears, which contains a Miner. After unlocking the cage and talking to the Miner, he will tunnel through the alternate path and lead the player to the Cave's portal.

sections.heading: Special Conditions
sections.text:
By beating the boss, the player may gain a condition according to the playing result in the Cave:
- If the player has never lost any health in the Cave, they will gain the Strong Body condition.
- On the other hand, if the player has used a revive in the Cave, they will gain the Frostbite condition.
- Using a revive before entering the Cave does not affect any result, such that it is still possible to get "Strong Body" as long as the player does not take health damage in the Cave.
- If the player loses health but doesn't die, they'll gain neither condition.
- If the player’s mount takes damage, they are still eligible for ‘Strong Body’. 
- The Freeze Buff can still extend freezing time on enemies. This is not affected by either condition.
- Neither condition can be obtained more than once in a looped run.
- On multiplayer, the status of all players is considered, and all of them will get the same condition, e.g.: if any player is revived, everyone will get 'Frostbite'.
- Losing health by the Pill's special ability is taken into account. However, Mysterious Trader is not subject to this.

sections.heading: Objects
sections.text: Crates look like boxes with an X shape on their top side. While most of the objects are similar with those in Glacier, there is a 1x1 stone pillar which is unique to this biome.

sections.heading: Temporary Buffs
sections.text: At least one random enemy in each room may drop a Temporary Buff. Picking this up will neutralize Freeze 3 times for 20 seconds. Cannot stack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This biome was added in Update 2.8.0.
- While playing in the Cave, an icy blue haze appears around the edge of game screen. Losing health causes the haze to briefly grow stronger, instead of causing the screen's edges to flash red temporarily like it usually would.
- This also occurs for other sources of health loss such as Pill and Breath of Hades.
- It is possible to find two chest rooms in the same floor while in this biome.
- The frozen surfaces in this biome show reflections. This even applies to Vampire, despite, well, being a vampire.
- This biome does not appear in the Sleepwalk challenge.
- Fishing was added to this biome as of Update 3.3.0.

sections.heading: Access
sections.text: Grave can be accessed if there is an extra passage in the boss room of the Relics biome - which has a 70% chance of being generated, accessible when the boss is beaten. The hallway leads to a room containing a puzzle. Interacting with the weird door will cause it to glow and for symbols to appear. The puzzle must be then solved within the time limit, as otherwise the tomb's access will be locked and can no longer be opened normally. The solution is connecting the symbols in a way that leaves no tile in the puzzle uncolored.

sections.heading: Special Conditions
sections.text:

- If the player has never lost any health, they will gain the Blessing Staff condition.
- On the other hand, if the player has used a revive in the Grave, they will gain the Curse of Grave Robbers condition.
- On multiplayer, the status of all players is considered, and all of them will get the same condition, e.g.: if any player is revived, everyone will get "Curse of Grave Robbers."
- Playing Little Commander and having revived minion of Necromancer killed will also trigger "Curse of Grave Robbers" even if none of the mercenaries fall.

- Primary: Fire a cannonball will explode upon contact with the Mist Dragon, and will deal more damage if more segments are hit.

- Secondary: Dismount from the cannon, the user will instantly switch to their other weapon.
- The player can also dismount by pressing the , or , with the Skill Button only being possible if the skill is not on cooldown.
- Being a weapon, Stone Dragon Cannon can be affected by buffs and status effects, such as Trumpet, and Stack Damage.

sections.heading: Hidden Entrance
sections.text:
There is a 70% chance for the 1-5 boss room to include an extra passage, accessible after defeating the boss. The passage leads to a puzzle room with a gate and five rune-engraved blocks arranged in front of it. Interacting with the gate activates the puzzle, revealing a 5x5 grid on the floor with 10 of the tiles marked with runes. After solving the puzzle, the gate slides down and opens a golden-colored portal, leading to the Grave biome.
- The markings on floor appear in pairs, and each rune block represents its corresponding marking.
- To solve the puzzle, the player is required to connect the 5 pairs of marks (nodes), fulfilling the following conditions:
- Each pair of nodes must be linked together.
- No links can intersect.
- The grid should have no empty tiles remaining.
- The node links can be controlled using the surrounding rune blocks. Interacting with them allows moving the link in four directions.
- The puzzle has a 90-second time limit. When the time runs out, the puzzle deactivates and the gate turns black. The deactivated gate cannot be opened through normal means.
- The glowing runes on the gate fade away as time passes. The number of runes visible acts as a makeshift timer for the puzzle.
- The player can force the gate open by using an attack dealing 500 or more damage in a single hit. Using this method opens the gate regardless of the state of the puzzle.
- Ancestor's Call strike can also open the door despite its attack dealing only 99 damage.

- The biome may be based on a Mayan/Aztec location, evident through the monkey statues and their presence.

Level Mode.lead: Level Mode is the main game mode of Soul Knight.

Boss Room.lead:
The HUD, or Heads Up Display, is a factor of a game where players can see their character's essential statistics.
In the game, the HUD includes a health bar, an armor bar, an energy bar, a counter of gold, and a mini-map with a dungeon level indicator. If the player plays as an upgraded Sword Master or Lancer, there will be a Sword Intent or Battle Will bar under the energy bar, respectively.

sections.heading: Player Vitals
sections.text:
The bars have fractions that show exactly the amount of a stat the player has. The health bar is red, the armor bar is gray, and the energy bar is blue. When the player loses health, armor, or energy, the color of the bar will drain, and the numerator will decrease based on how much the player lost. Some characters have their special resources and will be displayed below the energy bar. 
These stat bars will show an exclamation mark to the right, if:
- Health is below half of max value;
- Armor is depleted;
- Energy is below half of max value.
The gold counter is next to the pause button. It has a number showing the amount of gold the player has. It can decrease or increase as gold is collected or spent.
If Badass Mode is enabled, a purple monster icon will appear to the right of the stat bars.
If Boss Rush Mode is enabled, a red monster icon will appear to the right of stat bars.
If a challenge of Task Board is activated, the condition icons will also appear to the right of stat bars and the Badass icon (if enabled).

sections.heading: Mini-map
sections.text:
The mini-map shows the layout of the level a player is in.
The rooms are shown in squares and hallways are shown in rectangles connecting the rooms. The room the player is currently in will be whiter than the rest of the rooms. If there is a room that the player hasn't entered yet, it will be dark gray, but if they've entered it and left, it will be light gray.
There is also a dungeon level indicator below the mini-map, indicating which floor and level the player is in.

Enemies.lead:
Enemies are NPCs that the player must fight in the dungeon. Most of them deal damage, whereas some few heal other enemies or create new ones. Enemies spawn in enemy or boss rooms (except for Turret, Chester, and Mad Scientist). To pass the room, the player must defeat all enemies in it.
Enemies found in the last room of level X-5 are bosses. Bosses are more powerful enemies that block the way into the next level; a portal leading to the next level will spawn after defeating them.

sections.heading: Champions
sections.text:
Champions (sometimes known in-game as "elite enemies" or "elites") are larger and more powerful version of enemies. Champions have higher health, their attacks are usually enhanced, some Champions may have completely different behaviors. 
- They are more common in Badass Mode. They will always drop gold and energy (with a few exception, such as Crystal Beetles or Phantoms, which never drop gold), and are more likely to drop Materials on defeat (if they have a drop).
- Champions usually appear as a larger version of their normal self, with a purple aura. Champions in the Ancient Battleground are the only exception; they have a unique sprite but retain the size of their original version.
- Champions shared the same death counter as the base version in the Cellar and Soul Knight Handbook.
- Bosses may also appear as Champions. They are bigger in size, attack more frequently, have 25% more health (rounding varies with each boss), and drop more Materials on defeat but have the same attacks.

sections.text:
These rooms are Special Room with red entrances (since Update 1.5.1) and will not appear in the shortest path to the exit.
While these rooms are dangerous, chests containing weapons will appear to reward those wiping all the Champion enemies. The chests can be blue or golden as well as a green material chest.
- More reward chests will appear in Multiplayer, reflecting the number of players in the match.
- Usually, a level with 2 exclamation marks must have a Champion room.
- If the Genie Lamp condition is activated, a level with 3 exclamation mark rooms will have one.

Badass Mode.lead:
"Complete the game after unlocking everything in the living room to unlock Badass Mode."
Badass Mode is a difficulty in the game. The Badass Travel will allow the player to switch between levels of difficulty.

sections.heading: How to unlock
sections.text:
After unlocking every other Living Room extension, the player must reach level 4-6 and then interact with the Magic Stone.
The Badass Travel will then spawn in the Living Room, offering the player to switch between Normal and Badass Mode for the next run.

sections.heading: Statistics
sections.text:
- A purple monster icon will appear to the right of the status bars, similar to the icon shown in the minimap indicating a boss room.
- Enemies will spawn and attack more frequently.
- Champions spawn rate will increase.
- All bosses will always be champions, which means that they will have bonus health.
- Defense is lowered by 1. which means players take 1 extra damage from all sources, including enemy attacks, status effects and environmental damages.
- This is overridden by the challenge condition Shell Protection as all damage is still reduced to 1 for armor. Pets and followers take the usual damage as they don't have armor.
- Milk can completely nullify the effect.
- Armor Mounts will have 1 extra defense.
- Enemy projectile velocity greatly increased.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text:
- The player needs all possible methods to survive, especially when entering a room crowded with enemies near the door.
- Any buff that negates a damaging status effect is useful, as they will otherwise inflict effectively double damage.
- Choosing a weapon buff in early stages is not recommended, since it is likely the player will pick up different weapons later on.
- Maintaining Gold and Energy is not a big problem, since enemies (especially Champions) will drop more. Thus, the Sale Buff and Energy Orb Buff aren't as useful.
- If the player worries that they would die early, using the Gashapon Machine in the Living Room or watching TV in the Workshop to get a good weapon can help.
- The player may also forge weapons in the Workshop and get extra support in the Garden.
- Unless the player is confident of their "bullet hell" reading and dodging skills, a full defensive passive build is recommended.
- This includes statues like Statue of the Knight and Statue of the Paladin, and a fast melee (Meat, Nunchaku, etc.).
- Playing with a fixed D-Pad can be useful since it allows perfect movement.
- Getting Milk means everything will deal the usual amount of damage.
- Using an Armor Mount can be useful because they get 1 extra defense (in addition to their base defense stat, if any). Pairing them with Milk can result in taking 0 damage from most attacks.

Secret Rooms.lead: Secret Rooms are found randomly in different levels, their entrance and contents may vary depending on RNG, the Floor and the player's situation. If you're inside one your vision is limited just like the challenge condition Nearsighted.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.text:
Secret Rooms can appear once per Level on any Floor.
- If they appear on Floors 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5, the entrance will be through ladders or a staircase on the floor, initially hidden under a 2x2 square of boxes. This square spawns on locations that aren't part of the room's usual layout, and if the player is not in battle, the entrance will emit a faint glow that can be seen even through the boxes. Breaking the boxes will reveal the entrance, but is not required to actually access the Secret Room.
- The oxygen meter will still decrease in the Secret Rooms on the Undersea biome, with the underwater filter.
- If they appear in Monolithic Range Ruins on Floor 4, the entrance will be through the doorway of a dilapidated house localized on the top left of the room. During battle, said house will look like any other, but once the room is cleared, the inscriptions on the top of this house will regularly emit a yellow glow. In this state, approaching the structure will make its doorway glow, too, indicating that it can be entered.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.text: There are four different Secret Rooms available in the game:

sections.heading: Gold Room
sections.text: This Secret Room contains six Gold Mines that can be attacked, each dropping 10 coins. However, unlike regular Gold Mines, these will additionally spawn moving coins upon being destroyed. The coins bounce around the room and can be hit, which causes them to jump and drop even more coins. They disappear after a few seconds or if sufficiently damaged. They are immune to various status effects.

sections.heading: Mega Pill Room
sections.text:
This Secret Room contains ten Pills and a machine in the top middle. These Pills can be picked up and used as a weapon or consumed like normally, but when on the ground, they have collision and can be pushed around the room. The machine starts with a 0/5 count and Pills can be pushed into it. Inserting five Pills in the Mega Pill maker machine will cause it to spawn Mega Pill, and despawn any remaining Pills on the ground. Pills held by players or Followers are still kept.
- The collision of a Pill also affects other Pills, such that they can pushed into each other and, depending on how they were spawned inside the room, they may start moving immediately once the player enters, bouncing around on their own and pushing each other inside the Mega Pill Maker.

sections.heading: Legendary Buff Room
sections.text:
This Secret Room contains three pedestals, each holding a predefined Legendary Buff. The player can choose any of the three, causing the remaining two to despawn. Each of them comes with a special penalty that lasts for three battles, only after which the buff is functional.
The lists of buffs from left to right and the corresponding penalties given are:
- Tornado - Gives Debuff Speed Movement Speed -35%
- Frost Ring - Gives Debuff Fire Rate Fire Rate -50%
- Holy Nova - Gives Debuff Defense Defense -2
- Weapon Copy - GivesDebuff Fire Rate Fire Rate -50%
The "battles" refer to clearing a room, which includes not only enemy, boss or Elite rooms, but also Turrets Rooms.
- If the player is lacking any of the listed Buffs, the room can always appear. Any owned buffs cannot be taken again, as their slot are instead empty.

sections.heading: Combat Room
sections.text: This Secret Room is exclusive to Monolithic Range Ruins on Floor 4. It contains three pyres, each with a different flame color, difficulty setting and reward. The left one is orange, stating "Level of Difficulty 1, 120% more enemies."; the middle one is blue, stating "Level of Difficulty 2, 150% more enemies."; the right one is purple, stating "Level of Difficulty 3, 180% more enemies."

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- Secret Rooms were added in Update 5.3.0 along with Monolithic Range Ruins, being initially exclusive to Floor 4.
- The ground entrances were added in Update 5.5.0, allowing most Secret Rooms to be available on the other Floors. The Secret Room containing Pills and the Mega Pill Maker was added in this same update.

Portals.lead:
Not to be confused with Portal, an enemy found in the Mechanical Ruins.
Portals are swirling objects found at the end of each level or after defeating a boss. Interacting with them will cause the player to move onto the next level.
Going through a gate will reset the players' skill and statue cooldown, and restore their armor to full. It will also regular Mounts by half of their maximum health (or full if the Engineer is using an armor mount).
The Vampire as an NPC will open a Portal if he is unlocked and not being currently used. This method can essentially allow the player to completely skip an entire floor.
Portals are serve as checkpoints, so going back to the Main Menu and re-entering the game will revert to the situation the player had when they went through the last Portal. This can only be done once per Portal for balancing reasons.
If there are any Materials lying on the floor, the Portal must be interacted twice to enter. This is to indicate in case the player had missed any.
In Level Mode, if the boss in 3-5. is defeated, Inter-dimension Traveler (NPC) along with portal leading to 3-6 will spawn. Interacting with the npc will open the purple portal to 4-x the entry cost of 100 gold or 1 max hp (or free in Boss Rush)
- In Void Invasion, The Void leaves behind the purple portal leading to 4-x after it was defeated while Inter-dimension Traveler (NPC) spawns in a "!" room.

Turrets Rooms are rooms that can be found randomly at any level and offer items at the cost of a battle against turret enemies.

sections.heading: Room
sections.text:
They are indicated by a golden chest mark on the map. 
The rooms have two or more pedestals which may contain the following:
- A potion
- A seed
- A weapon up to rarity
- A Blueprint
- A random Material
Only one of these items may be chosen for free. However, every other platforms with unpicked items will transform into Turret enemies.
Room barriers will close during the battle.

sections.heading: Behaviors
sections.text:
Each Turret has 40 Health at level 1-X and it gains extra 15 Health after each floor, Turrets in level 2-X and level 3-X will have 55 and 70 Health respectively. 
- The Turrets' health is affected by the Double Joy.
- This apply to both type of Turret (normal and Rainbow Horse).
- This growing health factor carries over in Matrix of the Lord of Evil mode, resulting in an absurdly high health pool at high pressure level.
These Turrets will start attacking after roughly one second of delay as they rise from the ground. These turrets deal moderate damage and have a very high fire rate, firing large bullets that split into smaller ones and small, rotating, oval-shaped bullets in bursts.
If there are 3 turret stands, these turrets may be spawned as Unicorns instead. In this case, they will fire a rainbow laser, which does 2 damage on hit. The laser suspends itself for a period after firing, and when the attack is executed, a warning sound plays while a red aiming laser emerges, signifying the oncoming strike. Each defeated Unicorn turret has a slight chance of dropping a Rainbow Horse.
- Laser can increases the turret beam's width, although the laser will still deal damage.
- These rainbow horses are placed on Plunger pillars.
- When these turrets are destroyed, confetti appears for a brief second.
They come in three sizes:
- Small Turret Rooms (2 turret stands) will always contain a potion and a weapon. 
- Medium Turrets Rooms (3 turret stands) will contain a potion and two weapons. Occasionally, they will contain a Weapon Blueprint or material instead of a second weapon.
- Large Turrets Rooms (4 turret stands) will contain a potion, 2 weapons and another pedestal with seeds, materials or Weapon Blueprint.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text:
- The regular turrets can be very overwhelming by themselves, and nearly impossible to dodge when in groups. It is suggested to prepare a charge weapon as soon as the player grabs an item to hit the turret with maximum power.
- The unicorn turrets, on the other hand, are basically free sources of Rainbow Horses since they're just a cakewalk.
- If the player is low on Health, consider not grabbing any items and ignore the room.
- However, with good defensive weapons and the help of certain Buffs, Followers and/or Statues, taking a health potion or a strong weapon from the room can be worth the risk. Additionally, they drop plenty of gold and energy.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- The Turrets Room was added in Update 1.8.2.
- Unicorn turrets were added in Update 2.7.0.
- Before Update 1.8.5, Witch's Lightning Strike skill could not hit these turrets.
- Due to a bug, the turrets will still rotate even when Stun.
- The large oval bullets from the turret can push back the Assassin during his skill without dealing damage. This may be a glitch since he is supposed to be unable to be hit by any attack while dashing.
- Before a certain version in Multiplayer, when a player entered a turret room, any other players wouldn't actually be teleported to the same room, which would allow the others to enter the portal to skip an entire fight but still be able to obtain an item. This was an exploit that got patched.
- Also in Multiplayer, it's possible for different players to have different items if there is a blueprint that a player (or players) has but the rest do not. This means that the players that already have that blueprint can't get it again and are shown a different item.
- There is currently a glitch where a Turret converted into a Mummy/Frog by the Staff of Anubis will fail to close entirely upon defeat.
- This does not happen with Necromancer's upgraded Omen Stone skill, which transforms defeated enemies hit by the Plague into skeletons, or the Death Note, both which have similar effects to the Staff of Anubis in one aspect or another.

Scammer.lead:
The Scammer is an NPC that the player can encounter in the first room on a level. He usually appears on the upper-right side of the room. He cannot be found in Boss Rush Mode.
In most floors, he empties the player's last used Buff slot in exchange for gold, so that the player can choose a different Buff.
- He cannot remove the bonus Buff of fully-upgraded characters, or any other extra Buffs that do not occupy Buff slots.
- After paying him, the most-recent Buff will disappear immediately, including their effects.
- Upon entering the next floor, the player can choose a replacement.
- If a player is going to choose more than one Buff by removing more than one, the choosing will happen every time they move through a new Portal, until all Buffs are chosen. If multiple slots have been reset, it is possible to get two Buffs in the same floor by exiting and re-entering the current game.
- The gold price of the Scammer increases over floors. However, if the player is going to use a single Scammer more than once, the price will be doubled for each subsequent use, until moving to the next Portal where the Scammer's cost will reset.
- For example, in a certain floor the price is 14, 28, 56... but in the next floor the price might increase to 15.
If he is released from a Cage, he will provide an Amnesia Potion for free, which removes a Buff, but he can only provide once each time and this potion also fills up a Drink spot.
When the Scammer spawns at level 2-5/4-3/4-5/5-3 in Level Mode, he will offer some different Buffs in exchange of gold and 3 random Buffs that the player currently has (not including the Character's starter Buff).
- At level 2-5, the exchange price is 18, then 36 on the second deal, and 54 on the last exchange.

sections.heading: Quotes
sections.text:
- When the player decides to clear a Buff slot:
- "Lucky you"
- Talking to him after resetting all possible Buffs:
- "Too bad"
- If the player doesn't have enough money:
- "Goodbye”
- When the player releases him from a cage:
- "Lucky me"
- When he gives Amnesia Potion:
- "Here you go."
- When talking to him when he can exchange buffs:
- "See what you need."
- After the first, second and third buff exchange:
- "I see that you have an eye for things."
- "May Ares smile down on you."
- '"Writing your own destiny? Impressive!"

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- When first added, the Scammer could only remove a maximum of one Buff every time the player encountered him. 
- Before a certain version, the player wasn't able to reset more than one Buff in Multiplayer.
- In the Chinese translation, he is referred to as "Scheming Merchant," or "奸商," of which include merchants who scam.
- The Chinese quotes that he would say when rescued from a Cage are identical to the ones he says when the player pays him.
- After Update 5.0.0 the Scammer can exchange Buffs at level 2-5 in Level Mode.
- After Update 5.3.0 the Scammer can exchange Buffs at level 4-3 in Level Mode.
- After Update 6.5.0 the Scammer can exchange Buffs at level 4-5/5-3 in Level Mode.

Magic Stone.lead:
The Magic Stone is an etherial item and a pivotal element of Soul Knight.
It is found on level 3-6/4-6.
There are seven different colors of Magic Stone, according to the boss the player have defeated on level 3-5. The colors are as follows:
- Green for Volcanic Sandworm
- Red for Baby Dragon Bros
- Blue for Zulan The Colossus
- Purple for Varkolyn Leader
- Orange for Anubis
- Obsidian for Floating Laser UFO
- Cyan for Iron Pirate King Level and Iron Will Wavebreaker
The Magic Stone will also appear on the "Game Complete" sheet, along with the player's character, weapons, pets, buffs/drinks, total damage, kill counter and complete date.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
As explained in The Origin, the Magic Stone was a complete cluster of multiple colors and maintained the world's order. It was destroyed and fragmented in an alien invasion. As all efforts attempting to rewrite history would simply result in a temporal paradox where history merely repeats itself, the heroes are forced to recover them and restore relative order.
The High Priest (as well as some of the villagers) has dialogue about how he was overwhelmed by the Magic Stone's influence and created dangerous golems that destroyed his home.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- There were already four different colors of the Magic Stone, however, before Update 1.4.1, they were not related to bosses and would only appear at random.
- Since Update 1.8.0, the Magic Fragments the boss drops corresponds to the color of the Magic Stone obtained.
- After Update 2.2.0, the red and obsidian Magic Stone were added.
- The Magic Stone for Baby Dragon Bros before the update was orange.
- If the Magic Stone was reached due to the Vampire NPC spawning at 3-5 opening a portal, it will always be green.

Mysterious Trader.lead:
The Mysterious Trader is an NPC that can be found during a run.
He sells items such as Buff Bubble and Weapons.
Also, he can appear in a . In this case he will offer a random Buff or weapon at a reduced price.
The items in the shop cost 1 to 3 maximum HP limit. For each of the items purchased in the shop, the player's maximum Health will decrease by the items' costs. The player cannot purchase an item that has a cost equal to or higher than their maximum health.
- A Pill is sold for free at the first pad.
- The Sale can reduce the item cost by 1, but not less than 1 (unless he is rescued, such that price can be reduced to 0).
- Under the Exorbitant Price condition, the Buff bubble costs 2 HP limit, while the weapons cost 2-6 HP limit.
If a Buff is bought in this case, it acts as an extra Buff, and does not occupy standard Buff slots. Buffs that the player already owns will not spawn.
- In multiplayer, even though only the player who bought it will lose HP, everyone on the team is benefited by the acquired Buff.
He is the only source to get Strength Potion in a run, other than reforging.

sections.heading: Quotes
sections.text:
- When the player interacts with him:
- "See what you need"
- After being rescued from a Cage:
- "How is my hat?! How is my hat?!"
- Purchasing something after rescuing him:
- "You may need it."
- Not enough Health to afford:
- "It is... breathtaking"

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- This NPC was added in Update 2.2.0.
- When first added, his prices weren't affected by the Exorbitant Price condition.
- If the player doesn't have enough Max HP to buy an item, they will say "It is... breathtaking".
- In Chinese iteration, they will say "这东西要命了", which can be roughly translated to "This is lethal."
- There was a glitch that if a player bought a Buff and restarted the floor, the player could keep the Buff without losing maximum health.
- It was partly patched in Update 2.2.2 where the Buff would be lost if the game application had been restarted.
- In Update 2.2.6, it was completely patched.
- In Update 2.3.5, if the player only bought Buff Bubbles from this NPC, they only cost maximum health on the current level. Upon entering new levels, the maximum health would be recovered (but not the lost health). This glitch didn't occur if the player also bought a weapon.
- Buying items from him count as losing health. However, this is different from the negative effect of Pill which counts as "taking damage" instead.
- The Health Buff could be purchased from the Mysterious Trader for 1 max HP, effectively giving 3 max HP for free. Potentially, the player can purchase another 3-HP item from him, effectively gaining them without losing any max health.
- Before Update 2.5.5, Buff Bubbles would cost 3 max HP under the Exorbitant Price condition.
- Since Update 2.7.0, he appears with a small cloud raining above his head when seen in his shop.
- In Update 2.7.0, his prices were all 1 HP, but Strength Potion costed 2 HP. This bug was patched in Update 2.7.1.
- Since Update 2.9.0 where Strength Potion becomes a weapon, his shop may show the potion at first pad, while not selling any Buff Bubble in this case. Before that, his shop always contained one Buff Bubble.
- After Update 6.6.0, he will always sell 1 Pill at the first pad for free.

Kind Trader.lead:
The Kind Trader is an NPC that can be found during a run.
After completing the achievement "Buffed" which requires the player to obtain 20 different buffs, she can randomly appear inside a Chest Room.
She always displays 2 buff bubbles for sale at the cost of 1-2 max Armor, and only one Buff Bubble can be purchased, as the others will despawn. The player cannot acquire any of them if the value is equal to or higher than their max Armor.
- The 2-Amor Buffs are only on sale if the player already has the corresponding 1-Armor Buffs:
- Poison Stack requires Poison.
- Dragon Breath requires Fire.
- Frost Ring requires Freeze.
- Chaos Strike requires Elemental Staff.
Buffs that cost 1 Armor:
- Poison - Immune to poison gas and slow effect, increase poison damage to monsters
- Fire - Immune to fire, decrease explosion damage, and increase fire damage to monsters
- Freeze - Immune to freeze, and extra freeze time for the enemies
- Elemental Staff - Elemental bullets deal double damage on critical hit. Staff weapon deal higher damage
Buffs that cost 2 Armor:
- Poison Stack - Poison effect now can stack up to 3 times
- Dragon Breath - Release a conical Dragonbreath every 3 seconds
- Frost Ring - Gain 1 stack of Blockade every 10 seconds. Max 1 stacks. Each stack of Blockade can block one hit and release a Frost Ring
- Chaos Strike - After you cast the skill, your next attack will be strengthened and come with random elemental effect
If Kind Trader offers an owned buff (which can occur if it is acquired from another source on the same level, such as Mysterious Trader and Deelili Claw Fun), purchasing it deducts Armor, normally, but the acquired buff won't stack.

Followers.lead:
Followers are NPCs that follow the character around and assist the player by attacking enemies. They will draw enemy fire, and their attacks are more powerful than those of Pets. Followers will die and stop following once they run out of HP.
Unlike the player, Followers do not have invincibility frames, such that they can take damage from many enemy projectiles simultaneously.
Followers fall in the following three separate categories.

sections.heading: Temporary followers
sections.text:
This type of follower can only exist for a short amount of time or in the current floor. The following methods can summon Followers:
- Using weapons that have summon feature (for more details, visit the corresponding weapon page):
- Cannibal Plant - Summons a Titan Arum in every third attacks.
- Grave Guard's Hatchet - Summons 2 scarabs when the weapon is fully charged for the third time.
- Portable Bomber - Spawn a walking bomber for every 3 seconds.
- Scepter of Majesty - Summons a random robot knight in Chiseltown.
- Snowman Eagle - Summons tiny snowmen that last for 3 seconds upon critical hits.
- Staff of Anubis - Summons numerous mummy allies after the weapon absorbed enough souls.
- Staff of Illusion - Summons a copy of the character (two with Elemental Staff Buff).
- Staff of Skeleton - Summons skeleton soldier(sword and bow variants), summons giant skeleton if Elemental Staff Buff is present.
- Super Monster Card - Summons one of the 5 unique monsters to this weapon.
- Whisper of Dark - Has a 20% chance to spawn a skeleton soldier which can either wield a sword or a bow.
- Using certain skills & passive buffs (the Lone Wolf condition has no effect over them):
- Doppelganger (Assassin) - Summons a clone of Assassin.
- Gun Turret & Interceptor (Engineer) - Summons a gun turret or laser turret.
- Guardian Elf (Elf) - Summons elves to fight alongside.
- Frostfire Wolves, Venom Vines, Fuzzy Bear (Druid) - Summons wolves, vines and bear respectively.
- Nightmare, Omen Stone & Souls Resurrect (Necromancer) - Summons ghost hand, plague spider, and resurrects enemy.

sections.heading: Hiring
sections.text:
- In most cases, they can be found in special rooms in most levels. Note that these rooms cannot spawn with a Mercenary already present for the current floor.
- The room in which they appear will be indicated by a big yellow exclamation mark in the mini map, and possess appropriate decorations in most cases.
- Most Mercenaries can be hired at a cost of gold, which scales up with the level progression (15-30).
- This is affected by the Sale Buff and the Exorbitant Price condition.
- The cost does not increase in The Origin.
- Some mercenaries can also be rescued from a cage and hired for free, but are unarmed. If they survive the current floor, they will gain their default weapon in the next.
- The Mad Scientist is the only exception. If armed, he will be immediately hostile.
- Hiring a mercenary blocks their spawns in subsequent floors, effectively allowing only one at a time. Only after the current one is killed could more appear in the next floor.
- Cages are surprisingly exempt from this restriction, allowing the player to keep multiple mercenaries as long as they survive.
- It is possible to hire more than one mercenary in earlier iterations of The Origin, if the Summoner spawns one after another. The current one follows the same rules as in Level Mode, Matrix and Boss Rush.
- Some mercenaries can have multiple assist NPCs, which will also follow the player until death, upon which they simply despawn. They are always armed and are affected by Drillmaster upgrades, but cannot take other weapons.

sections.heading: Arming
sections.text:
- A mercenary comes with a default weapon, except Jim Smiley, who starts empty handed.
- Each mercenary has suitable weapon type(s), except Jim Smiley, who takes all standard weapons.
- By default mercenaries can only equip or lower rarity, except Pharaoh, who only use weapons, and Jim Smiley, who ignores this rule for the level the player recruits him.
- They can use higher rarity weapons, up to after they are trained by the Drillmaster, or if the player has the Pet Buff.
- All mercenaries can equip all Misc weapons (of all suitable rarities).
- Mercenaries cannot equip or these following weapons:
- Happy New Year
- Christmas Gift
- Scratch Card
- Super Monster Card
- Portable Bomber
- Strength Potion
- Captain's Medal
- Mercenaries also cannot properly use any of these weapons:
- Nirvana Cross
- Extra Crown
- One Punch (Legendary variant)
- To change their weapon, bring them to the weapon desired. If it is suitable, they will comment on the new weapon and equip it 2 seconds later. They will also drop their previous weapon.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
- The mercenaries tend to attack for a fixed period of time before pausing. This often results in them being unable to fully charge certain weapons, hence missing out on their benefits.
- Entering a new level will restore all mercenaries to maximum health.
- The Pet Buff increases all mercenaries' base HP by 35, and removes their weapon rarity restriction.
- Each Drillmaster upgrade increases all mercenaries' health by 15, and allow them to equip high rarity weapons.
- If the mercenary dies, the weapon they carried is lost with them.
- If they were observing a weapon when they die, they will somehow equip said weapon after 2 seconds, thus dropping their current weapon and making the other irretrievable.

- If set to Chinese language, he will comment on another character from the same game instead.
- Death: "...."

sections.heading: Soot Soot
sections.text:
- He has the appearance of a humanoid purple monster, with an apron and a chef hat.
- He may appear from a stone portal in a lone room by interacting with it.
- His basic health is 55.
- His default weapon is the Monster Cuisine.
- He can equip throwing weapons and railguns.
- However, with throwing weapons that have a melee function, he can only use the melee attack.
- Quotes
- Interaction: "Do you like Monster Cuisine?"
- Favor: "You are now my master!"
- Insufficient Money: "Can't even afford this?"
- Rescue: "You saw my bowl?"
- Suitable Weapon: "Is this edible?"
- Random Talking: "New ingredients to cook with!"
- Clearing Room: "What shall we cook today?"
- Death: "...."

sections.heading: Mad Scientist
sections.text:
- He looks like a typical crazy scientist from the movies: a long blouse, messy hair and a weird-looking face with rotating eyes.
- He appears beside a crashed desk which seems to be a time machine.
- His basic health is 55.
- His default weapon is the Crowbar.
- He can equip most Laser weapons, but not railguns.
- This is the only Follower that costs 0 gold to hire.
- There is a random chance that he is hostile, such that trying to hire him will reveal the fact and he starts to attack.
- If this happens, he becomes a 55-health enemy that can deal 4 damage, and will always drop 4 gold, 4 energy orbs and his Crowbar when killed. He takes damage from both players and enemies alike.
- Oddly, if an enemy kills him, he will still drop 4 energy and 4 gold, putting him in a weird limbo state of being damaged by both players and enemies.
- If rescued from a cage, he is friendly if unarmed, but hostile if armed.
- His quotes are full of symbols and gibberish.
- Quotes
- Interaction: "!@#$&^%×-/+{|"
- Hostile: "^%,\.]/×#@@?:|{</ | | "
- Favor: "(λ)"
- Rescue: "0x5330756C4B6E316768744E6F31......"
- Suitable Weapon: "!#@$%?"
- Random Talking: "^%,\.]/×#@@?:|{</ | | "
- Clearing Room: ":)&^$#@×&#"

sections.heading: Don Quixote
sections.text:
- He looks like a minor knight in level 2-x but with different helmet décor. He also appears to be wearing a horse outfit on his torso.
- If he is killed, the horse outfit's eye will be crossed out.
- He appears in front of a circus tent.
- He has an extremely high movement speed.
- His default weapon is the Retro Spear.
- He can equip spears, swords and bows.
- Quotes
- Interaction: "To surrender dreams - this may be madness."
- Favor: "Diligence is the mother of good fortune."
- Insufficient Money: "Perhaps to be too practical is madness."
- Suitable Weapon: "Who knows where madness lies?"
- Random Talking: "The wounds received in battle bestow honor."
- Death: "Until death it's all life."

sections.heading: Muscleman
sections.text:
- He looks like a soldier in green clothes and has golden hair.
- He appears below some palm trees.
- His default weapon is the Worn Bazooka.
- He can equip launchers.
- Quotes
- Interaction: "Live for nothing, or die for something."
- Favor: "Come with me if you want to live."
- Insufficient Money: "If you work for a living, why do you kill yourself working?"
- Suitable Weapon: "I was in charge of million-dollar equipment!"
- Random Talking: "I am here to chew bubble gum and kickass." (currently with a typo, should be "kick ass" instead)
- Death: "I will be back."

sections.heading: Shared Robot
sections.text:
- It looks like a one-wheeled black robot.
- It appears in a shared robot station, placed at the third slot. There is also a wrecked robot at the fourth slot.
- As the payment prompt displays when approaching the robot, simply interacting it will cause the player to hire the robot.
- Hiring this mercenary always costs half of the player's current gold, rounded down. Its weapon scales with the actual gold used, giving it a better weapon depending on how much the player spends.
- The gold used will determine the rank it becomes. This is shown in the favor text before the "protocol" word.
- With the Sale Buff alone, the price is reduced to one quarter of current gold while the Exorbitant Price condition means that hiring this mercenary depletes the player's gold reserves, or maybe left with 1 gold when hiring this with odd number of gold due to the rounded down mechanic before the condition applies. These will affect the rank.
- It is impossible to hire this mercenary if the player has less than 2 gold.
- The rank does not affect the health value of it.
- According to the rank of hiring, it may equip adjusted versions of these weapons with modified firing sprites.
- It will not take other weapons.
- Quotes
- Interaction: [Welcome to the shared mercenary station. Please insert [price] coins to hire one.]
- Favor: [Hire succeeded! Initiate the [rank] protocol.]
- Insufficient Money: [Payment failed!]
- Random Talking: [Beep Beep Beep. Enemies spotted.]
- Death: [Thank you for using our service. The debris will be decomposed in 886 years.]

sections.heading: Healing Knight
sections.text:
- He looks like a cleric in heavy plate armor, while carrying a giant cross.
- He appears in which seems to be a first aid camp, with three knights (wielding Staff of Light) assisting in saving some Royal Knights.
- Once hired, these NPC knights will follow the player until killed.
- His default weapon is the Hope.
- As with all NPCs, the Healing Knight only uses his weapon during combat, which means that he will not top up the player's health in between fights.
- He can equip staves.
- Quotes
- Interaction: "I hope you are surviving."
- Favor: "It seems that your situation is more urgent."
- Insufficient Money: "Can't go. I am on call."
- Suitable weapon: "It has my name on it."
- Random Talking: "I have your back."
- Death: "May there be no pain in heaven."

sections.heading: Pharaoh
sections.text:
- When found, he takes the form of a bone pile lying in the middle of a ritual circle. Once hired, he becomes a zombie with pharaoh decorations, and the candles in the circle will turn purple.
- After death, he will collapse into a bone pile again.
- When hired, the hero's Max HP is subtracted by 1-2, or 4 under the "Store price +100%" condition.
- The Sale Buff has no effect on his hiring cost unless the base value exceeds one.
- He cannot be hired if the player's max HP is too low or equal their max HP.
- His default weapon is the Pharaoh's Blade.
- He can only equip Legendary weapons. (Cannot equip the Strength Potion despite its rarity)
- Quotes
- Interaction: "The mummified body is longing for fresh blood..."
- Favor: "Well done for rewaking me!"
- Suitable Weapon: "This is the king's weapon."
- Random Talking: "I command you to lead the way."
- Encountering Anubis: "A king never hands over his fate to anyone."
- Death: "The power runs out."

sections.heading: Jim Smiley
sections.text:
- He looks like an old guy in a frog outfit.
- He may appear when the player uses Magic Well and Wishing Well, but the chance is low. Thus, technically he does not require a static amount of gold to hire.
- He can equip any weapon (except the above 7 misc weapons mentioned in Arming section.
- All his quotes are generally relevant to frog speech.
- Favor: "Ribbit~"
- Suitable Weapon: "Ribbit, Ribbit!"
- Random Talking: "Ribbit!"
- Clearing Room: "Ribbit, Ribbit, Ribbit!"
- Death: "Back to the pond..."

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
- All NPC followers that are also playable Heroes, spawned by summoning weapons/skills will not persist to the next floor.
- Royal Knight is the only mercenary with a defense value.
- Unlike all other Mercenaries, any assisting NPCs hired alongside him will not persist to later floors, even if they survive.
- Prior to Pharaoh and Jim Smiley's addition, no mercenaries can use weapons beyond purple Rarity without Drillmaster or Pet Buff's benefits.
- The Pharaoh is the only mercenary who carries a Legendary weapon.
- He is also the first mercenary to have a special quote at a specified condition. In this case, this is when encountering Anubis, the guardian of pharaoh.
- The Shared Robot is the only mercenary whose weapon and hiring costs are not fixed, as they scale on the amount of the player's funds, which in turn is dictated by a separate modifier.
- Technically, Jim Smiley costs are also not fixed, as he randomly appears from the Wishing Well and the Magic Well, the former costing gold to use while the latter is free.
- Due to an unknown glitch, followers spawned by staves don't attack or target the Training Dummy.
- All of Headgear Hero Follower regular quotes are kaomojis.

sections.heading: Update Trivia
sections.text:
- Update 1.5.0 added BarbarQ.

Boss Rush Mode.lead: Boss Rush Mode is a game mode in which the player will be fighting Bosses only.

sections.heading: Access
sections.text:
To unlock Boss Rush Mode, the player must:
- Unlock Magic Area.
- Meet Valkyrie during runs and buy 3 Feathers of Valkyrie from her.
After the player has met the two requirements above, Valkyrie will appear on top of the gravestone in the Magic Area, indicating that this mode has been unlocked.
The player can talk to Valkyrie and use one Feather of Valkyrie to open a red portal. Enter this portal to start a boss rush game. This can be done up to 3 times a day, and interacting with Valkyrie after completing 3 runs will cause her to say "You have used up your chances today, feel free to return tomorrow."
It is possible to start this mode with Challenge Conditions or Badass Mode, and most conditions will apply normally, except the following:
- Dungeon Expansion
- Genie Lamp

sections.heading: Rush to Purity
sections.text:
Rush to Purity is a modified version of Boss Rush Mode. 
For more information, see Rush to Purity.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
After interacting with the Valkyrie to activate Boss Rush mode, an icon of a red helmet will appear to the right of the status bar. Once the player enters the red portal, the Boss Rush game will start. If the player exits to the main menu or enters a regular game after opening the portal, neither the Feather of Valkyrie or daily attempt required to enter Boss Rush will be consumed.
Every Boss in this mode will be a Champion. If Badass Mode is enabled, an additional 20% HP increase (rounded up) is applied.
The mode has 3 floors devised into 13 levels, each floor has 4 levels with the third floor has 5.
- First floor includes a boss from Forest, Glacier, Relics, or Mecharuins (except for Goblin Priest (Haunted) and The Giant Of Dead Cells)
- Buff select after level 1-1, 1-2 and 1-4.
- Second floor includes a boss from Kingdom, Halloween, Dungeon, or Chiseltown
- Bosses from Cave, Swamp and Grave may also appear in this floor if the player has already beat them in Level Mode. The player will also get a random Challenge Conditions after defeat the boss even if they die or take health damage.
- Buff select after level 2-2 and 2-4.
- Third floor includes a boss from Volcano, Spaceship, or Neoisle (except for Iron Will Wavebreaker)
- The mode is completed when one reaches 3-5, where the Magic Stone is absent. Instead, the Valkyrie will appear on a large tombstone, with the clear time engraved on it.
- Fourth floor (optional) includes a boss from Monolithic Range Ruins, Ancient Battleground, or Undersea.
- Buff select when going into 4-1 and after 4-2.
Each level (except 3-5/4-5) will contain 5 rooms, layout in a plus shape:
- The South room is where the player started, indicated by on the mini map.
- A white Chest and a Gold Chest can be found in this room
- Other character NPCs, Vending Machines and the Scammer will not appear.
- The center room can be a chest room or a special room , which act exactly as those rooms would in a standard run.
- Not subject to Task Board conditions.
- The Special Room cannot be a Champion room. 
- The West and East rooms are filled with crates.
- The player can break these crate for energy or Health Pots if they had Crate Buff.
- The North room will contain a boss .
- Defeat the boss to open the portal to the next level.
- A Boss Rush chest will also appear.
- It will contain a random weapon (can be the boss's motif weapon) and a random small potion. This includes bosses found at 3-5 in Level Mode.

Buffs.lead:
For the exclusive Buffs in season modes, check the corresponding page.
See also: Drinks - Pet skills - Jewelry.
Buffs are passive abilities that are intended to boost the abilities and strength of players, weapons, and Followers to make the gameplay easier.

sections.heading: General
sections.text:
By default, players have a set number of empty Buff slots. As they progress in the run, these empty slots will be filled one by one after each Buff selection.
- In Level Mode and Boss Rush Mode, players have 7 empty Buff slots. In Matrix Mode and the Origin, they can have 38 and 10 empty Buff slots, respectively.
- Players can get additional empty Buff slots by having the Exceptionally Talented or Buff Slot +1 condition, consuming Tea, and harvesting Heptacolor Viola.
- They can lose a Buff slot by having the Buff Choice +1 condition.
- It is possible to clear Buffs and make them vacant again, starting from the most recently chosen. This can be done by using the Scammer, or by drinking Amnesia Potion. It will then become available for choosing before entering the next level.
Between some levels in a run, the player will be given the chance to choose a Buff among 3 randomly generated choices and will then occupy the empty Buff slot.
- The player can influence the number of choices at the Buff selection screen by having these conditions: Buff Slot +1 Buff Choice +1 Buff Buffet.
- The Buff selections will not appear when all available Buff slots have been occupied already. These Buff selections happen after passing some levels and are different in each Game mode.
- As long as there are more empty Buff slots than the amount usually at that level, be it by using Scammer or gaining extra Buff slots by Tea, Heptacolor Viola, or conditions, the player will be able to choose a Buff for the next level. Resetting the level will make the game check the number of empty buff slots again.
- If the empty buff slots are obtained in the Living Room, the player can make a buff selection after selecting the floor to start from and before entering the level.
Each character has a Passive Buff which can be unlocked by upgrading a character to level 6. Once unlocked, this Buff will fill in the first star slot. This Buff complements the character's playstyle and cannot be removed by any means.
Apart from the aforementioned slots, additional Buffs can also be gained during a run. Gaining Buffs through this method will not occupy any free Buff slots, and cannot be removed in the current game.
- Taking the Mentor buff (from Mentor) and the Magic Well buff (from the Magic Well in the Garden).
- Using certain plants in the Garden, see Planting for details.
- Picking up Buff Bubble which will contain a random Buff inside. They can be bought from:
- Mysterious Trader at a cost of 1 ...

sections.heading: Buffs on NPCs
sections.text:
Some Buffs can also apply to friendly NPCs such as Pets and Followers. Mostly, these are Buffs that affect weapons, since they can also affect the weapons of the followers.
- Affect weapon used by Followers: Accuracy - Bounce - Combo - Laser - Melee Range - Reflect - Shotgun
- Directly affect Pets or Followers: Pet - Pet Charge - Pet Mimic
NPCs summoned from Skills or Weapons such as Staff of Illusion can have special Buff interaction.

keyword_snippets.text: The bars have fractions that show exactly the amount of a stat the player has. The health bar is red, the armor bar is gray, and the energy bar is blue. Champions (sometimes known in-game as "elite enemies" or "elites") are larger and more powerful version of enemies. Champions have higher health, their attacks are usually enhanced, some Champions may have completely different behaviors.

- They are more common in Badass Mode. They will always drop gold and energy (with a few exception, such as Crystal Beetles or Phantoms, which never drop gold), and are more likely to drop Materials on defeat (if they have a drop).

- Champions usually appear as a larger version of their normal self, with a purple aura. Champions in the Ancient Battleground are the only exception; they have a unique sprite but retain the size of their original version.
- Champions shared the same death counter as the base version in the Cellar and Soul Knight Handbook.

- Bosses may also appear as Champions. They are bigger in size, attack more frequently, have 25% more health (rounding varies with each boss), and drop more Materials on defeat but have the same attacks.
- In Badass Mode, Boss Rush Mode, or under the Full Alert condition, they will always be Champions.
While these rooms are dangerous, chests containing weapons will appear to reward those wiping all the Champion enemies. The chests can be blue or golden as well as a green material chest.
- More reward chests will appear in Multiplayer, reflecting the number of players in the match.
- Usually, a level with 2 exclamation marks must have a Champion room.
- Attacks deal damage and reduce the player's energy. Projectiles are blue.
